Repeatedly selecting variants and checkpoints on one validation sample creates selection bias; ordinary confidence intervals do not remove it. [Cawley–Talbot](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf) and [adaptive holdout research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629) motivate limiting validation feedback. Practical protocol here: predeclare trial budget, checkpoint evaluation cadence, patience and tie-breaking; count checkpoint comparisons as selection opportunities; log every attempted variant. Keep independent host test evaluation for the frozen winner. Reusable-holdout methods require controlled feedback, so their guarantees cannot be claimed for unrestricted repeated HR@10 queries.

Recommended uncertainty analysis: save each user’s binary hit for baseline and variant; bootstrap the same user indices for both models, separately within each dataset, retaining 200 draws per category. For each replicate, average the four category mean differences with weight 1/4; report the macro difference, percentile interval and category differences. This measures user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates; it excludes training-seed and negative-sampling variability and does not correct adaptive selection. [Recommendation significance research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02461) supports bootstrap/randomization methods, although its large-sample findings do not guarantee calibration at 200 users.

Use matched SASRec ablations: identical splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, candidate sets, checkpoint policy and comparable compute; change one component at a time. Report all four categories and the prescribed macro HR@10; avoid category cherry-picking or interpreting tiny gains as established improvements. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled rankings can reverse full-catalog conclusions: retain the pinned 99-negative evaluator, but describe results specifically as sampled HR@10.
